issue.title: Add a non-failing finalizer refusal policy so a bad refuse is not always terminal
issue.description:
## Feature proposal

`finalizers.instances.<id>.refusal` currently accepts only `"fail"`
(`src/sase/finalizers/config.py`). `dispatch_commit_decisions` converts any refusal
into a terminal `BuiltinCommitFinalizerError`, which always strands a held workspace.

Add a softer policy (for example, accept the refusal, leave the tree dirty, and
release the workspace) so a bad or overly-cautious refuse is not always fatal.

This was deliberately out of scope for plan:202608/finalizer_recovery_evidence.md:
it is a config-schema change with wire implications, and the tale only gave the
recovery turn enough evidence to stop refusing on false "I have no context" grounds.

task_type_fields.proposal: Extend finalizers.instances.<id>.refusal beyond fail so dispatch_commit_decisions can accept a refuse, leave the tree dirty, and release the workspace.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: plan:202608/finalizer_recovery_evidence.md forbids changing refusal policy; it is a config-schema change with wire implications.

payload.description: A refuse is still always terminal even after recovery evidence lands
